# Quantum Bus Parallelism

**How does the number of shared harmonic modes limit a layer of independent entangling gates?** This project derives a mode–force–time law for closed geometric gates generated by commuting linear conditional forces, and quantifies the drive and displacement exposure needed when the bus is damped.

For a lossless bus, $`K`$ disjoint maximally entangling pairs, $`m`$ physical modes, and a per-qubit force bound $`g`$, the optimal duration obeys

```math
T_\epsilon(K,m,g)
=\Theta_\epsilon\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+K/m}}{g}\right).
```

The corresponding minimum force-fluence action is

```math
\mathcal A_\epsilon(K,m)
=\inf T\int_0^T\sum_{j,\ell}|u_{j\ell}(t)|^2\,dt
=\Theta_\epsilon(K+K^2/m).
```

These statements hold for every fixed whole-layer **half-diamond error** $`0\le\epsilon<1/\sqrt2`$, while requiring exact spin–bus disentanglement. The lower bound permits final local $`Z`$ corrections and every equivalent phase wrap. An explicit zero-error construction attains the scaling in the independently controlled force model. With vacuum Markov loss, the account derives the full damped channel, necessary bounds on noisy gate accuracy, and the exact drive–exposure frontier for a specified phase matrix.

| Mode budget at fixed force per qubit | Independent-pair layer duration |
|---|---|
| A fixed number of modes | Grows as $`\sqrt K/g`$ |
| An intermediate budget $`m\le K`$ | Scales as $`\sqrt{K/m}/g`$ |
| A number of modes proportional to $`K`$, or larger | Scales as $`1/g`$ |

A collective interaction can occupy one geometric direction even when it couples many pairs. A layer of disjoint gates imposes a different constraint, preserved by the gate-equivalence and fixed-error arguments below.

## Learn the project

The single educational anchor is **Häffner, Roos, and Blatt, _Quantum computing with trapped ions_ (2008)**, [Physics Reports 469, 155–203](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physrep.2008.09.003). Its account of motional modes and geometric phase gates provides the physical starting point.

The [source-to-project bridge](learning/HAEFFNER_BRIDGE.md) supplies focused reading pointers, translates notation and assumptions, and works through a complete closed-loop gate before connecting it to the parallelism problem. The [30-milestone map](learning/MILESTONES.md) organizes the learning route into background/preliminaries and narrative/innovation. It is a common understanding map for any reader.

The review supplies the physical foundations. The bridge connects those ideas to the lossless bounds, damped trajectories and resource accounting; the scientific pages give the complete statements and proofs.

## Reproduce the checks

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -r verification/requirements.txt
python3 verification/run_all.py
```

The deterministic checks cover Fourier constructions, phase-wrap robustness, general spectral controls, the damped channel and drive–exposure examples. The [verification guide](verification/README.md) describes the committed reference output and the scope of each check. Universal and asymptotic claims are established by the analytical proofs.

## Physical scope

The number $`m`$ counts dynamical oscillator modes, not drive channels or waveform tones. The force budget is the squared norm summed over modes for each qubit. It is an effective Hamiltonian resource, with a device-dependent conversion to actuator amplitude or physical energy.

The upper construction requires independent complex forces, adequate modulation bandwidth, and oscillator excursions compatible with the harmonic approximation. Restricted hardware inherits the lower bound when it fits the model; it need not attain the upper bound. The lossless result concerns commuting conditional-force gates with exact bus disentanglement for any initial oscillator state. The loss analysis assumes vacuum initial modes and fields, common-rate Markov damping, and compensated trajectories that close exactly. Its resource frontier fixes a full phase matrix and optimizes paid force fluence versus exposure; it does not optimize full noisy-gate error. Other interaction mechanisms and intermediate noncommuting spin control require separate resource analysis.

Spectral area inequalities and parallel-gate constructions have substantial precedents. The [attribution account](references/related_work.md) identifies the inherited ingredients and places the robust, gate-equivalence-invariant converse within that literature.
